target: Espero que a internet funcione no hotel.
english: I hope the internet works at the hotel.
tip: 'Esperar que' (to hope that) triggers the subjunctive – it expresses an uncertain wish.
Object pronouns go before the verb here: 'te amo', not amo-te. Front placement is the norm in spoken Brazilian.
'De carro' means by car. Portuguese uses 'de' for transport: de onibus, de aviao, but 'a pe' for on foot.
'Gostar' always takes 'de' before what you like: 'gostam de samba'. Dropping the 'de' is wrong.
'Com educacao' literally means with education but here means politely: 'corrigiu com educacao' = corrected politely.
Spoken Brazilian uses the bare verb for commands: 'traz' instead of the textbook 'traga'. Both mean bring.

target: Eu vou ligar para você mais tarde.
tip: Spoken Brazilian favors ir plus infinitive for the future: vou ligar, not the stiffer written ligarei.
'Nas' fuses 'em + as' (in/at the): 'nas festas' = at the parties. Portuguese contracts em with articles: em+os=nos, em+a=na.
'Pagar com' means to pay using a method: 'pagar com Pix'. To pay for an item, switch to 'pagar por'.
'Pedir' takes its object directly with no preposition: 'me pediu um favor', unlike English ask for.
'Dever' plus a noun means to owe: 'te devo um favor'. Before a verb, 'dever' means should: devo ir.
'Esperar' means wait for and needs no preposition: 'te espero' = I wait for you. Portuguese omits the for.

english: I thought you were very funny.
tip: 'Achar' means to find in the opinion sense: 'te achei engracado' = I found you funny. Use it for impressions.
'Convencer' links to the next verb with 'a': 'convenceu a ir' = convinced to go.
'Duvidar que' expresses doubt and triggers the subjunctive: 'terminem', not terminam.
'Embora' (although) always takes the subjunctive: 'embora tenhamos' = although we have.
'Do' is 'de + o' (of the): 'endereco do restaurante' = the restaurant's address. Portuguese shows possession with 'de', not an apostrophe.

target: Ele me emprestou o carro dele.
tip: 'Dele' means his and follows the noun: 'o carro dele' = his car. It is clearer than the ambiguous 'seu'.

target: Ela nos emprestou o apartamento dela.
tip: 'Emprestar' means to lend, not to borrow: 'nos emprestou' = lent us. For borrowing say 'pegar emprestado'.

target: Ele me deu um conselho valioso.
tip: 'Conselho' is countable here: 'um conselho' = one piece of advice. English advice cannot be counted that way.

target: A gente nos reuniu para comemorar.
tip: 'A gente' means we but takes a singular verb: 'a gente reuniu', like ele. Very common in everyday speech.

target: Eu te dei a minha palavra.
tip: Brazilians often keep the article before a possessive: 'a minha palavra' = my word. Dropping it is also correct.

target: Talvez ele precise de mais tempo.
tip: 'Precisar' takes 'de' before a noun: 'precise de mais tempo' = needs more time. Skipping the 'de' sounds off.

target: Paga a conta antes de sair.
tip: 'Antes de' plus an infinitive means before doing: 'antes de sair' = before leaving. With a full clause use 'antes que'.

target: É preciso que você faça o cadastro online.
tip: 'E preciso que' states a need and triggers the subjunctive: 'faca', not faz.

target: Antes que eu me esqueça, parabéns pelo aniversário.
tip: 'Antes que' takes the subjunctive: 'antes que eu me esqueca' = before I forget.

english: I'll bring you a little souvenir.
tip: The ending '-inha' is a diminutive, small or affectionate: 'lembrancinha' = a little souvenir, from lembranca.

english: I admire him for his courage.
tip: 'O' is him as a direct object and sits before the verb: 'eu o admiro' = I admire him. Casual speech says 'admiro ele'.

english: She reminded me of the appointment.
tip: 'Lembrar de' means to remind of or remember: 'me lembrou do compromisso' = reminded me of the appointment.

english: It's possible that it rains tomorrow.
tip: 'E possivel que' triggers the subjunctive: 'chova', not chove.
